newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds down again, gains in unlinked bonds.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds down again, gains in unlinked bonds.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed down on Thursday as CPI-linked bond prices continued to fall on expectations for a low September consumer price index and on profit taking, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.1 pct to 165.86
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: unchanged at 157.71

"Trading today was a continuation of the trend of the last few days, where after rising considerably (in the past month) CPI-linked bonds are going through a period of calm," said Hanna Pri-zan, manager of the securities department at Bank Hapoalim.
"This is caused by profit taking, expectations for a low CPI and because yields are at quite a low level," she said.
Yields on long-term CPI-linked bonds have fallen from 5.25 percent at the end of August to 4.7 percent and on short-term bonds from 5.2 percent to 4.5 percent, traders said.
September's CPI will be published on October 15.
Demand for unlinked bonds continued to be strong, Pri-zan said. "Most of the Treasury's new issues are in these bonds, which present a wide range of possibilities and high yields," she said.
Prices of dollar-linked bonds were unchanged, Pri-zan said, after strengthening on Wednesday.
Elisha Rosenfeld of Lehava Investments said prices in the longer term CPI-linked bonds fell more than the short-term ones in which trading was mixed.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
